messages:
nora: heads-up — saw a spike in fncall schema rejections this morning from retail-ingest. Console shows 'rejected' but the sample payloads are clearly tool-run outputs that are just arrays vs objects. it looks like the validator is strict and the routing fallback (degen variant) is triggering, but the dashboard lumps them as 'errors' which confuses product and billing.
mike: can you paste an example? curious if it’s a harmless pluralization mismatch or something else.
sasha: quick note — we recently rolled the stricter fncall validator in canary for eu-west at 2am. fallback to cheaper model variant is enabled for strict rejects.
nora: example from the log:
```
validator: {"error":"invalid_shape","details":"expected object at top-level, got array","response_sample":"[ { \"id\": 123, \"text\": \"ok\" } ]" }
```
nora: the call itself succeeded and produced reasonable content. but because the adapter expects {items: []} we treat it as a fncall rejection, route to degen, and the console shows a hard red error count.
albert: that explains the surge we saw in the dashboard. product flagged an SLA regression. they assume we are dropping requests, not degrading model variant.
janet: is the billing for these routed->degen flows counted toward the original route's quota or the fallback? product needs clarity.
mike: currently billing attribution uses the final model route id. so if it fellthrough to degen, the cheaper model gets charged. but we increment the 'validation_reject' counter on the canonical route (the one that originated the fncall) which is what the console surfaces as an error.
sasha: so two separate signals: charge goes to fallback model, errors go to orig route. that mismatch is definitely confusing.
deploy-bot: deploy 1713000200-fncall-validator-v2 -> succeeded (canary eu-west)
nora: proposal A: change console UX to show 'soft-reject / fallback' as its own status (amber) instead of hard error — show both origin route + final charge model in the message.
albert: proposal B: don't increment 'validation_reject' metric for shape mismatches that are resolved by harmless coercions (we need a whitelist). instead tag them as 'soft-coerce' with a small penalty but not an alert.
janet: product asks: do we count soft-coerces against quota? their use-case is sensitive to token spend and they want predictable quotas.
mike: imo we need a config knob per-route: `treat_fncall_shape_mismatch_as` = [reject|soft|coerce]. default for enterprise accounts should be 'soft' with opt-out. also surface the effective setting in the console per-route.
sasha: telemetry-wise we should add tags: fallback_reason (enum: validation_shape, timeout, denoising), origin_route_id, final_model_id, counted_for_billing=[yes/no]. that will make dashboards queryable.
janet: +1 on tags. also add a sample of request/response in the console popover (redacted) so support can triage without poking logs.
albert: operational alert idea: if soft-fallback rate > 5% over a 15m window for a route, page oncall with a short summary and top samples (s3 link). otherwise just traffic to the 'soft' metric.
nora: one UX wrinkle: current rollout policy automatically flips traffic to the cheaper variant when strict-validate rejects exceed threshold. for this class of harmless shape mismatches we should not auto-flip. that caused product surprise.
mike: agree — change rollout to exclude 'soft' reasons from the auto-flip calculation. auto-flip should only use fatal rejects and latency-induced fallbacks.
sasha: implementation notes: validator needs to emit reason codes and a 'coercion_suggestion' field when applicable. adapters need a tiny bit of code to detect array-vs-object and try a coercion path (wrap array -> {items: array}). we can keep coercion off by default but on for enterprise.
janet: timeline: product wants the console change + tags in telemetry within 2 sprints. billing policy doc update and the per-route knob in 3 sprints.
albert: quick follow-up question — for audit/billing clarity, if we don't count soft-coerces toward orig-route quota, will any customers complain that their logical operation failed even though they got a result? we should surface that in the console explicitly.
mike: add clear language: "This request fell back to an alternative model to preserve correctness; charging applied to final_model_id. The originating route saw a soft-validate event and may be reported for observability only." put links to billing docs.
nora: action items:
  - S1: telemetry: add fallback_reason/origin_route_id/final_model_id/counted_for_billing tags (sasha)
  - S1: console: add 'soft-fallback' state + popover with origin+charge info + sample (janet)
  - S2: validator: add reason codes + coercion_suggestion (mike)
  - S2: adapters: implement optional coercion wrapper + opt-in flag per-route (albert)
  - S2: billing: draft policy for soft-coerces (janet + finance)
  - S3: rollout: exclude soft reasons from auto-flip (mike)
sasha: I'll open tracking tickets and add the new telemetry schema. will ping when PRs land.
janet: I'll update the console mockups and product notes; will route to legal for billing language.
nora: thanks all. if someone hits >10% soft-fallback on a route before we land this, please @ops and drop top 3 samples in the thread so we can triage quickly. :thumbsup:
mike: noted. adding an alert rule to the monitoring board with the 5%/15m threshold.
deploy-bot: alert-rule created: monitoring/soft-fallback-rate -> threshold 5% / 15m (owner: eng-oncall)
nora: perfect, closing for now.
